prerequisites: Knowledge from "Grundlagen der Elektrotechnik 1" and "Mathematik 1 für E/Me" or corresponding modules from other study programs with equivalent content and scope.

learning_outcomes.text: Students who have successfully studied this module can describe electrical and magnetic fields. Based on this, they possess the necessary fundamental knowledge about the behavior of passive electronic components required for calculating electrical networks with time-varying voltages and currents. They can extend what they learned in "Grundlagen der Elektrotechnik 1" to AC applications.

After successful completion of the module, students are able to describe the behavior of passive electronic components under time-varying excitation. They apply fundamental mathematical procedures for network calculation with time-sinusoidal excitation.
Students who have successfully completed this module correctly apply important calculation procedures for the analysis of AC circuits with time-sinusoidal periodic excitation.

Students who have successfully completed this module can exchange ideas with other students about the questions they need to work on and can organize corresponding collaboration among themselves. They can appropriately summarize the results of their experimental work in a short report.

syllabus_topics: Sinusoidal alternating quantities and their representation
Slowly time-varying magnetic field (Law of Induction, self- and mutual inductance)
assessment_rules: Graded assessment is by a written exam (Klausur), details according to the valid study regulations. Ungraded assessment is by experimental work, consisting of approximately 5 experiments, each lasting 90 minutes. For ECTS credit points, both graded and ungraded components must be completed.
bibliography: T. Harriehausen, D. Schwarzenau: „Moeller Grundlagen der Elektrotechnik", Springer Vieweg
